Latin word

afficiō

afficiō, afficere, affēcī, affectum

verb, third conjugation (-iō): with the accusative, often with an ablative of the state produced

affect, act on (body or mind); affect, have an effect on (someone)

In this lexicon

  • affect

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 16.4.1: variē sum adfectus tuīs litterīs; Liv. 28.15: famēs sitisque corpora adficerent (Lewis & Short)

  • effect

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 5.20.6: nūllā umquam voluptāte tantā sum adfectus

Examples

  • Variē sum adfectus tuīs litterīs, valdē priōre pāginā perturbātus, paulum alterā recreātus.

    Your letter affected me in two ways: the first page upset me badly, the second cheered me up a little.Cic. Fam. 16.4.1

    In the entry for affect

  • etsī graviter prīmō nūntiō commōtus sum

    although I was badly shaken by the first newsCic. Fam. 3.10.1

    how I wept at your hymns and songs, deeply moved by the voices of your sweetly singing church!Aug. Conf. 9.6.14
